workouts.title: Joint Awakening Flow
workouts.description: Loosen every major joint before training. Follow the beginner warm-up movements.

exercises.name: Neck & Shoulder Rolls
instructions: Stand tall, feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed.
Roll the shoulders backward 8 times, then forward 8 times.
Gently circle the head: chin to chest, ear to shoulder, both directions.
Keep the breath slow and even throughout.

exercises.name: Hip & Waist Circles
instructions: Hands on hips, feet a little wider than shoulders.
Draw big circles with the hips — 8 clockwise, 8 counter-clockwise.
Keep the upper body relatively still; the motion is in the pelvis.

exercises.name: Arm Swings & Twists
instructions: Let the arms swing freely across the body, twisting gently at the waist.
Allow the heels to pivot naturally with each swing.
Build a relaxed, rhythmic momentum for 40 seconds.

workouts.title: Foundational Stances
workouts.description: The roots of Shaolin: Horse, Bow, and Cat. Taught here by Shaolin Temple instructors.

exercises.name: Horse Stance (Ma Bu)
instructions: Step wide, about twice shoulder-width, toes pointing forward.
Bend the knees and sink straight down as if sitting on a stool.
Keep the back upright, chest open, and weight even on both feet.
Rest the hands in fists at the waist. Hold and breathe into the Dan Tian.

exercises.name: Bow Stance (Gong Bu)
instructions: Step one foot forward into a long stance.
Bend the front knee over the ankle; keep the back leg straight and strong.
Front foot points forward, back foot angled out about 45 degrees.
Square the hips forward and hold. Switch sides halfway.

exercises.name: Cat Stance (Xu Bu)
instructions: Bring the feet close, weight almost entirely on the back leg.
Front foot rests lightly, only the ball of the foot touching.
Sink down on the back leg, staying light and ready on the front.
Hold with calm, alert posture. Switch sides halfway.

exercises.name: Five Stances Form (Wu Bu Quan)
instructions: Flow through the five basic stances as a short form.
Move slowly at first, settling fully into each stance.
Coordinate the breath with each transition.
Repeat the sequence on both sides.

workouts.title: Ba Duan Jin — Eight Pieces of Brocade
workouts.description: The classic eight-movement health Qi Gong, practised for over 800 years. Gentle, complete, and deeply restorative. Follow along with the full routine on each step.

exercises.name: 1 · Two Hands Hold Up the Heavens
instructions: Stand relaxed, feet shoulder-width. Interlace the fingers in front of the belly.
Inhale and raise the joined hands overhead, turning the palms to face the sky and stretching upward.
Exhale and float the arms back down to the sides. Regulates the Triple Burner.
Repeat slowly several times.

exercises.name: 2 · Draw the Bow to Shoot the Hawk
instructions: Sink into a Horse Stance.
Extend one arm as if holding a bow; the other draws back as if pulling the string, gaze along the 'arrow'.
Alternate sides smoothly. Opens the chest and strengthens the lungs.

exercises.name: 3 · Separate Heaven and Earth
instructions: From standing, press one palm upward to the sky and the other downward to the earth.
Stretch gently in both directions, then switch hands.
Harmonises the spleen and stomach.

exercises.name: 4 · Wise Owl Gazes Backwards
instructions: Stand tall, arms relaxed at the sides.
Slowly turn the head and gaze back over one shoulder without moving the torso, then the other.
Relieves tension and 'the five strains and seven impairments'.

exercises.name: 5 · Sway the Head and Shake the Tail
instructions: Sink into a wide Horse Stance, hands on thighs.
Circle the torso, bending toward one side then the other in a slow, relaxed arc.
Cools excess 'heart fire' and calms the mind.

exercises.name: 6 · Two Hands Hold the Feet
instructions: From standing, fold gently forward and slide the hands down the backs of the legs toward the feet.
Rise slowly, sweeping the hands up the front of the body.
Strengthens the kidneys and the lower back.

exercises.name: 7 · Clench Fists and Glare Fiercely
instructions: Sink into Horse Stance, fists at the waist.
Punch slowly and powerfully forward, alternating, with a fierce, focused gaze.
Builds strength and circulates Qi and vitality.

exercises.name: 8 · Bouncing on the Toes
instructions: Stand tall, heels together, arms relaxed.
Rise onto the balls of the feet, then let the heels drop with a gentle bounce.
Repeat seven times. Shakes out tension and 'a hundred ailments'.

workouts.title: The Five Animals (Wu Xing)
workouts.description: An introduction to the five animal spirits of Shaolin — Tiger, Crane, Leopard, Snake, and Dragon — each cultivating a different quality. Study the demonstration, then explore each shape.

exercises.name: Tiger — Bones & Strength
instructions: The Tiger trains the bones and raw power. Tiger-claw hands, low rooted stances.
Move with heavy, committed force from the waist and back.
Cultivates strength and fearless spirit.

exercises.name: Crane — Sinews & Balance
instructions: The Crane trains the sinews, balance, and calm spirit.
Stand tall on one leg; the arms become long, light wings.
Move softly and precisely, cultivating poise and patience.

exercises.name: Leopard — Speed & Power
instructions: The Leopard trains speed and concentrated power.
Use the leopard-paw fist; strikes are fast, sharp, and explosive.
Cultivates quickness and aggressive intent.

exercises.name: Snake — Qi & Suppleness
instructions: The Snake trains internal Qi, breath, and flexibility.
The body flows and coils; the fingers strike like a serpent's head.
Move smoothly with the breath, cultivating sensitivity and softness.

exercises.name: Dragon — Spirit (Shen)
instructions: The Dragon trains the spirit and flowing, undulating power.
The waist leads; the whole body moves as one connected wave.
Cultivates presence, focus, and the unity of body and mind.

workouts.title: Bodyweight Strength & Conditioning
workouts.description: Classic bodyweight conditioning to build the foundation of relaxed power.

exercises.name: Push-ups
instructions: Hands under the shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower with control until the chest is just above the floor.
Press back up, keeping the core braced and hips level.
Drop to the knees if needed — quality over quantity.

exercises.name: Horse Stance Hold
instructions: Return to Horse Stance and sink low.
Hold steady, breathing slowly, for the full duration.
Feel the legs build heat — this is the forge of the Shaolin body.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squats
instructions: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sit the hips back and down, keeping the chest up and heels planted.
Drive through the floor to stand. Move with steady tempo.

exercises.name: Plank
instructions: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Straight line from head to heels; brace the core and glutes.
Breathe steadily and hold without letting the hips sag.

workouts.title: Opening & Flexibility
workouts.description: Gentle stretches to open the hips, hamstrings, and spine for kicks and low stances.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold
instructions: Feet hip-width, soft knees.
Hinge at the hips and fold forward, letting the head hang heavy.
Relax the neck and breathe into the back of the legs.

exercises.name: Deep Lunge Hip Opener
instructions: Step one foot far forward into a low lunge.
Drop the back knee toward the floor and sink the hips down.
Keep the chest lifted; feel the front of the back hip open.
Hold, then switch sides at the halfway point.

exercises.name: Seated Wide-Leg Stretch
instructions: Sit with legs spread wide and comfortable.
Keep the back long as you fold gently forward from the hips.
Never force — breathe and ease a little deeper with each exhale.

workouts.title: Cool-down & Settle
workouts.description: Bring the heart rate down and gather the energy back to the center.

exercises.name: Gentle Spinal Twists
instructions: Stand or sit tall, arms loose.
Slowly rotate the torso left, then right, following with the gaze.
Move with the breath — inhale center, exhale twist.

exercises.name: Standing Dan Tian Breathing
instructions: Stand relaxed, palms resting over the lower belly.
Breathe slowly and deeply into the Dan Tian.
Feel the warmth of the practice settle and gather inward.
